title: Predation of Lycorma delicatula White (Hemiptera: Fulgoridae) by web-building spiders associated with anthropogenic structures
content:
Abstract
Spotted lanternfly, Lycorma delicatula White (Hemiptera: Fulgoridae), is an invasive species that originated in Asia, and has recently invaded the United States of America. L. delicatula has a broad host range, resulting in damage to cultivated and wild host plants and nuisance issues for homeowners and businesses. There is limited information regarding predators of L. delicatula in the United States, but strong interest from the public on how populations of this invasive species can be reduced using natural methods. Therefore, we recorded spiders found around anthropogenic structures that may serve as predators of L. delicatula. We documented presence of L. delicatula in all spider webs observed around anthropogenic structures in monthly surveys in 2023 (adults only), and 2024 (nymphs and adults). We also introduced L. delicatula to webs in both years to measure both web ensnarement and fate of L. delicatula. Four families of spiders were documented; Agelenidae, Theridiidae, Pholcidae, and Araneidae with significantly more L. delicatula observed in Agelinidae funnel webs compared with other families and web types in both years. L. delicatula was observed in 15.0% and 9.2% of all webs in 2023 and 2024, respectively. When L. delicatula was introduced into webs, the only families with web-types that retained and with individuals who were observed feeding on L. delicatula were Araneidae (2023 only) and Theridiidae (2023 and 2024). Overall, our findings suggest that spiders contribute to mortality of L. delicatula and may play an important role in reducing nuisance issues caused by L. delicatula in and around anthropogenic structures.
